ColPali: Efficient Document
Retrieval with Vision Language Models

The paper introduces ColPali, a retrieval model that leverages Vision Language Models to generate contextualized embeddings directly from document page images, addressing the limitation of modern systems that struggle to exploit visual cues. Combined with a late interaction matching mechanism, ColPali largely outperforms modern document retrieval pipelines while being drastically faster and end-to-end trainable, as demonstrated on the new ViDoRe benchmark.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01449v3

Problem & Motivation

  • Modern document retrieval systems excel at query-to-text matching but fail to exploit visual cues such as tables, figures, and layouts, hindering performance on practical applications like Retrieval Augmented Generation.
Motivation
  • Addressing this gap is crucial because visually rich documents are common in real-world industrial settings, and efficient retrieval from them can unlock knowledge sources previously difficult to index or query.

Method Overview

  • ColPali adapts PaliGemma-3B to generate ColBERT-style multi-vector representations of text and images, using a projection layer to map output embeddings to a reduced dimension D=128, and is trained with an in-batch contrastive loss and late interaction scoring.
  • The training set comprises 127,460 query-page pairs from academic datasets (63%) and synthetic VLM-generated pseudo-questions (37%), with models trained for 1 epoch using LoRA adapters (α=32, r=32).
  • The method leverages the alignment between text and image token embeddings from multimodal finetuning, and empirically validates max-pooling over sub-page chunks for pagewise embedding.

Key Idea / Formula

ColPali's core mechanism is a late interaction matching between query text embeddings and document page image patch embeddings, both produced by a Vision Language Model (PaliGemma-3B) that projects SigLIP-So400m/14 patch embeddings into Gemma-2B's text vector space. This design enables end-to-end trainable retrieval that directly exploits visual cues from page images, addressing the limitation of text-only retrieval systems that struggle with visually rich documents.

Main Experimental Results

  • ColPali achieves the best overall document-retrieval performance on the ViDoRe benchmark, with notable NDCG@5 improvements over strong baselines, particularly on visually complex tasks such as InfographicVQA, ArxivQA, and TabFQuAD.
  • The method also outperforms text-image embedding models and captioning-based baselines across all evaluated domains and languages.
  • Experiments on ViDoRe, a comprehensive benchmark covering diverse document types, validate the claims.
  • The results show consistent improvements across all domains, with particularly large gains on infographics, figures, and tables, supporting the paper's claim that visual context is key for document retrieval.

Contributions

  • The paper introduces ViDoRe, a comprehensive benchmark for visually rich document retrieval, and ColPali, a novel retrieval model that generates multi-vector embeddings purely from visual document features using a generative vision-language model.
  • ColPali outperforms existing document retrieval methods while enabling faster indexing and low querying latencies, and the authors release the benchmark and models to foster future work.
  • Innovation: The novelty lies in applying a generative vision-language model to create multi-vector embeddings directly from page images, bypassing the need for OCR or layout analysis.
  • This approach leverages the latest VLM capabilities to handle diverse modalities (figures, tables, infographics) and demonstrates strong performance on the new ViDoRe benchmark, which itself is a contribution as it repurposes existing QA datasets and adds new practical datasets.
